levelSpawnOverride.note: The level's Spawn1 serializes no RuntimeLocations and no RuntimeLocationLookups (property indices 0 and 1 absent), so the ship uses the Blueprint template's slots unchanged. Its 28,541 bytes are the attached actors (413), the 16 height maps, the 32 octrees, the navigation location and component flags. The OutpostExport decode stops after 35 bytes because the 2.00 class has one property the usmap lacks before AttachedActors (a single soft path, here 'PersistentLevel.Collision'), which shifts every later index by one.

hydra.name: Hydra

forms.note: Only a balancing asset exists (Enemies/Kebab/Missile/DataAssets/DA_Balancing_C_Kebab_Missile): no enemy type, Blueprint, mesh or group table names a Missile Hydra in 2.00, so it never spawns from these files.

where.onFrigate: The Frigate's AI manager spawns its 'turret' enemies from TurretReinforcements = EGT_StaticWorld_Kebab (one Hydra per group) through hatches of TurretHatchClass = BP_Frigate_KebabHatch.
where.slots: Spawn_Kebab (14), Spawn_Kebab_BreachableCore (2), Spawn_Kebab_CargoLatch (4), Spawn_Kebab_CargoLatches_Finished (2): 22 places on the ship.
where.inferred: That those four Spawn1 tags are the manager's TurretSpawnTag, TurretSpawnTag_BreachableCore, TurretSpawnTag_CargoLatch and TurretSpawnTag_CargoLatches_Finished: the property names match the tags one to one, but the data asset leaves those four names at their class default, and class defaults (script) are not in the paks.

howMany.why: No count is in the files: the manager has no maximum for turrets (only MaxNumActiveCouriers and MaxNumActiveAirToGrounds), and the runtime fields (NumPendingTurretSpawns, TurretSpawnPointQueue, TurretControllerSpawnIndices) are filled by code. Each spawn point is an FBookablePoint with its own Hatch and an UnlockedBy (EFrigateEmplacementUnlockedBy, values not in the files).
howMany.upperBoundInferred: one Hydra per Spawn_Kebab* slot at most (FBookablePoint can be booked once), 22 slots

trigger.puzzle: Tied to the puzzle by name: the tag suffixes BreachableCore, CargoLatch and CargoLatches_Finished name puzzle pieces of the ship (BP_Frigate_BreachableCore, BP_Frigate_CargoLatch x4), and each spawn point records what unlocked it (FBookablePoint.UnlockedBy, EFrigateEmplacementUnlockedBy).
trigger.inferred: Hydras at the 2 BreachableCore slots appear when the breachable core is breached, at the 4 CargoLatch slots when the cargo latches are worked on (4 slots, 4 latches), and at the 2 CargoLatches_Finished slots once all latches are released; the 14 plain Spawn_Kebab slots are the base set. Only the names say this; the logic is script code.
trigger.alsoInferred: The AI manager component tracks FrigatePuzzleProgress, PuzzleStepCompletedVelocityBonus, PuzzleProgressVelocityBonus and DesiredAIThreatLevel, so the spawning pace follows puzzle progress (field names only).

hatch.blockDeployablesInferred: the hatch has a LocalBlockDeployable component attached under a 300 cm sphere: players cannot place deployables on a closed hatch (component name only)
hatch.animation: HatchAnimation opens the bones BaseCover_01.. with the curves Curve_LS_Kebab_01_Base_Open_0N

emerge.how: The Hydra waits inside its hatch. Its Emerge capability (group Part.Capability.Turret.Emerge, ability GA_Kebab_Shared_Emerge, which owns the tag Ability.Turret.Emerge while active) starts when its utility reaches 0.8 and stops below 0; the utility is its alertness through the curve [[0,0],[0.18632028,1],[1,1]] (0 at rest, 1 from alertness 0.19 up). The hatch opens while its occupant has Ability.Turret.Emerge (OccupantDeployedTag) and closes 2 s after it is gone (CloseDelay).
emerge.inferred: So a Hydra pops up as soon as it notices a player (alertness about 0.15 gives utility 0.8) and sinks back when it calms down; the guns fire only in combat, each 2 s after the Hydra entered that alertness state (utility curve [[1.9,0],[2,1]]).

dying.inferred: while dying it keeps Ability.Turret.Emerge for 2.5 s, so it stays raised for its death

balancing.unitsNote: the game's own balancing units (part health), as gamedata/arc/enemy-balancing.json reads them; not hit points per player shot

turrets.note: the three stacked gun turrets (Part.Decorator.ID.Joint, segments Top, Middle, Bottom); they break off when destroyed (DismembermentSetup: Joint parts, ProbabilityOfBreakingOff 1)

weakPoints.note: one per turret (Part.Decorator.ID.Core, resistance group WeakPoint)

parts.killRule: Destroying all three turrets kills it: the HealthService chain event 'TurretsKillFrame' destroys the Frame when every Part.Decorator.ID.Joint is below 1% health.
parts.stuns: Each segment (Top, Middle, Bottom) is stunnable on its own, armour excepted (StunsDefinition, propagation per segment).

damagePerHit.inferred: the damage effect GE_RifleProjectileAbilityDamage multiplies the firing part's PhysicalDamage by 1, and the balancing's only damage row is 1 (Blunt) for the gun segments (ID.Segment); so 1 balancing damage unit per bullet

aimTurnRateDegPerS.note: the top segment's articulated aiming (turret yaw, guns pitch); the other segments have their own definitions

attacks.dispersion: BP_ConstructableDispersionServiceAutomaticRifle: accuracy worsens against dodge rolls (-1), crouch or slide (-0.2), fast targets and far targets (curves), with box shapes that shrink as it keeps hitting
attacks.fireRateWhy: the rate and burst lengths are in the turret state machine's time transitions (CSM_Kebab_Gatling_Turret), which keep their class defaults: not in the paks

ranges.note: Sight: 65 m (lost at 80 m) out of combat, 120 m (lost at 150 m) in combat, 180 degree cone; long-range hearing. The sense configs need a Part.Decorator.ID.Sensor part, and CSSC_Kebab_Gatling maps no bone to ID.Sensor (the Emerge capability also requires one): how the Hydra senses without that part is not in the files.

barrage.targets: the ground, never the ship: grid positions with nav NONE( Enemy.Navigation.Frigate )
barrage.summary: A 4 x 4 grid of 16 m cells (64 m square) laid on the densest cluster of players 100 to 200 m away, shelled row by row: one shell every 0.35 s, 0.5 s between rows, after windups 0.25 s apart and a 1.75 s pause. Each shell explodes in an 8 m radius for 75 explosive damage (the balancing row for its Eye part), with shockwave falloff. It holds fire around ARC Reclaimers (7 m).

behaviour.note: Its Primary (barrage) and Emerge capabilities both score the Frigate's cargo progress (BT_FrigateCargoProgressUtility, bInvert true, Progress left at its default) and Emerge also the Frigate's movement state (BT_FrigateMovementStateUtility, bInvert true). EFrigateCargoProgress's values are not in the files.
behaviour.inferred: the cannon emerges and shells the ground around the ship while the cargo run has not reached its default progress stage and while the Frigate is not in its default movement state (the inverted utilities); which stages those are is not in the files
